skill.name: deploy-to-vercel
skill.description: Deploy applications and websites to Vercel. Use when the user requests deployment actions like "deploy my app", "deploy and give me the link", "push this live", or "create a preview deployment".
skill.summary: Guide Vercel deployments through Git, authenticated CLI commands, or temporary deployments without login.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: All 68 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, documentation links, error redirection, or deployment account checks. Two semantic risks remain: indiscriminate Git staging and deployment paths that can publish production without explicit production approval. No evidence found of malicious exfiltration or audit-directed prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The Git workflow stages every local change before committing and pushing.
remediation.suggestion: Review changed and untracked files, check for secrets, and stage only approved paths before requesting approval for the exact commit and destination.

remediation.issue: Git pushes and temporary deployments can publish production despite the stated preview default.
remediation.suggestion: Check the current branch against Vercel production settings before pushing. Use a preview branch, and require explicit production approval before temporary deployments.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Git Staging Can Publish Unreviewed Files
semantic_findings.description: The approved push workflow runs "git add ." before committing and pushing. Without reviewing changes, this can publish unrelated work or unignored secrets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly stages every change under the current directory without a diff or secret review. Push approval does not identify the staged contents.

semantic_findings.title: Production Deployment Paths Bypass The Preview Default
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires previews unless production is requested. Its Git workflow pushes the current branch without checking production settings, and its no-auth fallback uses a temporary production URL.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly says production branches deploy production, but the push steps never check the branch. The temporary fallback also explicitly describes production deployment.

content.value_statement: Vercel deployments require different steps depending on Git integration, project linking, and authentication. This skill guides deployment selection, team setup, and deployment URL reporting.
actual_capabilities: Check Git remotes, local Vercel linking metadata, CLI authentication, and available teams.
Select Git push, direct CLI deployment, or a temporary deployment based on project state.
Guide team selection and project linking with team-scoped CLI commands.
Request approval before committing and pushing changes to trigger Git deployments.
Retrieve deployment URLs and inspect build status through the Vercel CLI.
Report temporary deployment claim links and expiration information returned by the CLI.
limitations: Requires shell access, network access, and an available or installable Vercel CLI; it provides instructions rather than bundled deployment scripts.
Temporary deployments are documented as unavailable in CI and directories already linked to Vercel.
Does not verify deployed pages through HTTP requests or browser testing.
Does not enforce preview routing on Git pushes or temporary deployments, and its Git example stages all local changes.

use_cases.title: Share A Feature Preview
use_cases.description: Deploy an approved feature branch through an existing Vercel Git integration and retrieve its deployment URL.

use_cases.title: Set Up Team Deployment
use_cases.description: Select a Vercel team, link a local project, and choose an appropriate deployment method.

use_cases.title: Publish A Temporary Demonstration
use_cases.description: Use the no-login fallback for a non-sensitive demonstration, then report its claim link and expiration.

prompt_templates.title: Check Deployment Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this project's Git remote, Vercel linking state, authentication, and teams. Recommend a deployment method without changing files or deploying.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the project before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy A Linked Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this linked project as a preview using the Vercel CLI. Confirm the target team and report the deployment URL and build status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: deploy a linked project without a Git remote.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy Through Git
prompt_templates.prompt: Review changed files and stage only approved paths. Confirm this is not the production branch, then request my approval before committing and pushing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: trigger a preview through an existing Git integration.

prompt_templates.title: Use A Temporary Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Check temporary deployment eligibility and confirm no sensitive files will be uploaded. I approve a temporary production URL; report its claim link and expiration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: deploy without login when the documented restrictions permit it.

best_practices: Review changed files and secrets, then stage only approved paths before authorizing a Git push.
Confirm the target team, project, and production branch before deploying; require explicit approval for production or temporary production URLs.
Inspect build status and keep temporary deployment claim links private.
anti_patterns: Running the broad Git staging example without reviewing unrelated changes and unignored secrets.
Assuming every Git push or temporary deployment produces a preview environment.
Treating a returned deployment URL as proof that the application builds successfully or works correctly.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Actual deployment requires the environment to provide the necessary shell and network permissions.

faq.question: Do I need a Vercel account?
faq.answer: Standard linking and deployment use Vercel authentication. The skill also describes a temporary deployment fallback without login.

faq.question: Does it always create preview deployments?
faq.answer: No. Although previews are the stated default, pushing a production branch or using the temporary fallback can create production deployments.

faq.question: Will it commit and push my changes?
faq.answer: The Git workflow requests approval before committing and pushing. Its example stages all local changes, so review files and narrow staging first.

faq.question: How does it choose a Vercel team?
faq.answer: It reads linked organization metadata or lists available teams. It asks when multiple teams are available and otherwise uses the single destination.

faq.question: Does it test the deployed website?
faq.answer: No. It reports deployment URLs and can inspect build status, but explicitly avoids fetching the deployed URL for verification.
